blocks.content: Chandigarh's culture chapter blends its Punjabi cultural inheritance with a distinctive planned-city civic culture found nowhere else in India — a duality that shows up often in exam questions contrasting 'traditional' and 'modern' Chandigarh.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India's rich cultural tradition includes 8 major classical dance forms recognized by Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.
Harvest and seasonal festivals such as Bihu (Assam), Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Onam (Kerala), and Baisakhi (Punjab) reflect the agrarian roots of Indian heritage.
Key premier cultural institutions include the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), Sangeet Natak Akademi, Lalit Kala Akademi, and Sahitya Akademi.
India's UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage items include Durga Puja of Kolkata, Garba of Gujarat, Vedic Chanting, Ramlila, and Kumbh Mela.

blocks.content: Chandigarh's cultural fabric is predominantly Punjabi in flavour — cuisine, music, dress, and festival life closely mirror the wider Punjab region, a natural consequence of the city's founding population of Partition refugees and continuing migration from Punjab and Haryana.

At the same time, as a purpose-built modern capital, Chandigarh has developed its own distinct 'civic culture' around its planned public spaces — the Leisure Valley, Sukhna Lake promenade, and Sector 17 Plaza function as genuinely new kinds of shared public/cultural space rarely found in organically grown Indian cities.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Rose Festival at Zakir Hussain Rose Garden is one of the most distinctively 'Chandigarh' cultural events — tying the city's horticultural planning heritage directly into its festival calendar.

items: Punjabi cuisine dominates — tandoori dishes, butter chicken, chole bhature, sarson da saag with makki di roti, and lassi are all closely associated with the city's food identity, especially around Sector 17 and Sector 35 markets.
Chandigarh's dhaba (roadside eatery) culture, radiating outward along the highways connecting to Punjab and Himachal Pradesh, is a well-known regional food institution.

State-wise matching questions on folk dances, classical dances, and harvest festivals (e.g., Sattriya to Assam, Mohiniyattam to Kerala, Pongal to Tamil Nadu) are extremely high-yield in UPSC, SSC, and State PSC exams.
Be prepared for questions regarding recent additions to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list and World Heritage Sites in India.
Note the apex bodies governing Indian culture and their headquarters, particularly the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) under the Ministry of Culture.

items: Culturally, Chandigarh is predominantly Punjabi — Baisakhi and Lohri are the major traditional festivals.
Rose Festival (Zakir Hussain Rose Garden) and Mango Festival are Chandigarh's distinctive horticulture-linked cultural events.
Government Museum & Art Gallery, Sector 10, was designed by Le Corbusier himself.
International Dolls Museum, Chandigarh — one of the largest of its kind in Asia.
